outputs.L1: The invention relates to a puncturing system comprising an outer tubular body configured to remain within a body part of a living being. The puncturing system is characterized by at least one inner tubular body and a puncturing needle, wherein the inner tubular body is guided through a working lumen of the outer tubular body and is longitudinally displaceable relative to the outer tubular body. The puncturing needle is guided through a puncture lumen of the inner tubular body, and the inner tubular body is longitudinally displaceable relative to the puncturing needle. After the body part has been punctured by a puncturing section of the puncturing needle protruding from a patient-side end of the puncturing system, the inner tubular body can be advanced beyond the patient-side end of the catheter and at least partially out of the outer tubular body. The inner tubular body is thereby configured to accommodate, at least partially within its puncture lumen, the puncturing section of the puncturing needle protruding from the patient-side end of the catheter.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a puncture system that includes an outer tubular body intended to remain within a body part of a living organism. The system further comprises at least one inner tubular body and a puncture needle. The inner tubular body extends through a working lumen of the outer tubular body and is longitudinally movable relative to it. The puncture needle passes through a puncture lumen formed in the inner tubular body, which is also longitudinally movable relative to the needle. Once the body part has been pierced by a puncturing section of the needle projecting beyond the patient-side end of the system, the inner tubular body may be advanced from the patient-side end of the catheter so that it emerges at least partly from the outer tubular body. In this position, the inner tubular body is configured to receive, at least partially within its puncture lumen, the projecting puncturing section of the needle.
outputs.L3:
The puncturing system comprises an outer tubular body configured to remain in a body part of a living being during use. The outer tubular body defines a working lumen through which an inner tubular body extends. The inner tubular body is longitudinally movable relative to the outer tubular body and, in turn, defines a puncture lumen through which a puncturing needle passes. The inner tubular body is also longitudinally movable relative to the puncturing needle.

After the puncture has been performed, the inner tubular body can be advanced beyond the patient-side end of the outer tubular body. In this extended position, the inner tubular body at least partially encloses the puncturing section of the needle that protrudes from the outer tubular body. The puncturing section is thereby received within the puncture lumen of the inner tubular body, which may help shield the needle after puncture.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a puncturing system designed to improve safety when a tubular body is retained in a patient after a puncture procedure. The system includes an outer tubular body, an inner tubular body disposed within the outer tubular body, and a puncturing needle extending through a lumen of the inner tubular body. The outer tubular body is configured to remain in the patient and may provide an access path for subsequent treatment, drainage, fluid administration, instrument insertion, or another medical procedure.

The inner tubular body is movable in the longitudinal direction relative to the outer tubular body. During puncture, the puncturing needle is guided through the lumen of the inner tubular body, with a puncturing section of the needle projecting from the distal end of the system. This projecting section allows the needle to penetrate the target tissue and enables the outer tubular body to be placed at the desired location.

After the puncture has been completed, the inner tubular body is advanced distally relative to the outer tubular body. In its advanced position, the inner tubular body extends beyond the distal end of the outer tubular body and surrounds the puncturing section of the needle that would otherwise remain exposed. The protruding needle section is thereby enclosed within the lumen of the inner tubular body.

Covering the puncturing section reduces the risk that the needle will unintentionally damage tissue while the outer tubular body is being retained, adjusted, or otherwise handled. The arrangement therefore permits the outer tubular body to remain in the patient while limiting exposure to the sharp portion of the needle. As a result, the system provides safer and more reliable retention of the outer tubular body following puncture.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to something specific—a person, place, object, or idea already known or clearly identified. There is a difference between “a book” and “the book”: the first could be any book, while the second refers to one particular book.

Although “the” often goes unnoticed, it brings clarity and precision to communication. It guides readers, creates shared understanding, and gives importance to what follows. This simple three-letter word demonstrates how even the most ordinary parts of language can have an extraordinary impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a puncturing system with an outer catheter, a longitudinally movable inner tube, and a puncture needle that can be retracted into the inner tube after puncturing.
counterfactuals.output: A puncturing system includes an outer catheter defining a longitudinal lumen, an inner tube disposed within the lumen and longitudinally movable relative to the outer catheter, and a puncture needle associated with a distal portion of the inner tube. The inner tube is movable between a puncturing position, in which a distal tip of the puncture needle projects beyond a distal end of the outer catheter, and a retracted position, in which the distal tip is received within the inner tube. Following puncture of a target tissue, the puncture needle is retractable into the inner tube to shield the distal tip while the outer catheter remains positioned across or adjacent to the target tissue. The system may include an actuator, stop, or locking mechanism configured to control relative movement of the outer catheter, inner tube, and puncture needle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in formal patent language where an outer tubular body remains in the patient, an inner tubular body slides through its working lumen, and the inner body encloses the exposed puncturing section of a needle after use.
counterfactuals.output: A medical access device comprising an outer tubular body configured for placement through tissue and retention within a patient, the outer tubular body defining a working lumen extending between proximal and distal ends thereof. An inner tubular body is slidably receivable within the working lumen and is movable between a retracted position and an advanced position. A needle is associated with the inner tubular body and includes a puncturing section configured to project distally beyond the inner tubular body during insertion of the medical access device. Following puncture and placement of the outer tubular body, the inner tubular body is movable relative to the needle such that the puncturing section is received within and enclosed by the inner tubular body. The inner tubular body and the enclosed puncturing section are thereafter removable through the working lumen while the outer tubular body remains positioned in the patient to provide continued access to a target site.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph independent patent claim for a catheter-based puncture device comprising nested, longitudinally displaceable tubular bodies and a needle, emphasizing post-puncture needle shielding.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A catheter-based puncture device comprising: an outer tubular body having a distal end and a lumen; an inner tubular body coaxially disposed within the lumen and longitudinally displaceable relative to the outer tubular body, the inner tubular body defining a needle lumen and having a distal shielding portion; a needle disposed within the needle lumen and longitudinally displaceable relative to the inner tubular body, the needle having a distal puncture tip; and an actuation assembly operatively coupled to at least one of the outer tubular body, the inner tubular body, and the needle, the actuation assembly being configured to place the device in a puncture configuration in which the distal puncture tip projects distally beyond the distal shielding portion and, following puncture of tissue, to cause relative longitudinal displacement between the needle and the inner tubular body to place the device in a shielded configuration in which the distal puncture tip is enclosed within the distal shielding portion, wherein the actuation assembly includes a retention feature configured to resist distal re-emergence of the distal puncture tip from the distal shielding portion after the device enters the shielded configuration.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert these design features into a European patent-style invention summary: an indwelling outer tube, a movable inner tube having a puncture lumen, and a puncturing needle whose patient-side tip can be received inside the inner tube after puncture.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a puncture device comprising an indwelling outer tube, an inner tube movably arranged relative to the outer tube and defining a puncture lumen, and a puncturing needle extending through the puncture lumen. The puncturing needle has a patient-side tip configured to perform a puncture and subsequently to be received within the inner tube. Retraction of the needle tip into the inner tube after puncture shields the tip while the outer tube remains indwelling, thereby reducing the risk of unintended contact with the needle tip.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a technical description of a medical puncturing system designed to reduce injury risk by advancing an inner tubular member out of an outer catheter so that it accommodates the protruding puncture section of the needle.
counterfactuals.output:
A medical puncturing system includes:

- a **puncture needle** having a distal puncture section, such as a sharpened needle tip;
- an **outer catheter** defining an axial lumen through which the needle is inserted; and
- an **inner tubular member** disposed movably within the outer catheter and having a lumen capable of receiving the puncture section.

During puncture, the needle extends distally beyond the outer catheter to penetrate tissue or a vessel. After puncture, the inner tubular member is advanced in the distal direction relative to the outer catheter. Its distal end projects from the outer catheter and surrounds or otherwise accommodates the portion of the needle protruding from the catheter. The puncture section is thereby isolated from surrounding tissue while the catheter assembly is advanced, positioned, or manipulated.

The inner tubular member may be actuated by a proximal slider, hub, spring mechanism, or other drive element. Stops or locking features can define its retracted and advanced positions and prevent unintended re-exposure of the needle tip. By covering the sharp puncture section before or during catheter advancement, the system reduces the risk of vascular-wall injury, tissue laceration, accidental needlestick, and damage caused by contact between the exposed needle and adjacent anatomical structures.
